title: ADNP loss produces a CHD4-like sparse chromatin program in thalamic, midbrain, hindbrain, and Pvalb neurons
exact_observed_result: Adnp perturbation produced a sparse multi-cell response: 25 FDR genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, three in 155 MB Glut, two in 191 MB P MY GABA, and one in 052 Pvalb Gaba. Cacnb3 rose recurrently, Plppr3/Atp9a fell in midbrain and thalamic contexts, and the 151/155 score vectors placed Chd4 as the nearest non-self Adnp neighbor.
biological_interpretation: The signal fits a ChAHP-biased ADNP/CHD4 chromatin branch, but the measured transcriptome is sparse and cell-context-gated rather than a broad ADNP-loss collapse.

support.description: Adnp generated a 151 TH chromatin response and recurrent Cacnb3/Plppr3/Atp9a markers; Chd4 was its nearest non-self signature neighbor in 151 and 155.

caveats: Adnp self-transcript rows were nominal at best; none of 21 self rows passed FDR.
Arid2 diverged from the strongest thalamic Adnp response and should be treated as a negative comparator, not a driver.

prior_expectation.summary: ADNP is an autism and intellectual-disability chromatin factor and can recruit HP1 and CHD4 in the ChAHP complex, creating a direct prior for ADNP-CHD4 convergence.

citations.citation: Helsmoortel et al., Nature Genetics, 2014. PMID:24531329.
